description: Split one PDF into several PDFs, either by explicit ranges (each comma group becomes one part: "1-2,3-5" gives two parts) or into fixed-size chunks (every=2 on 5 pages gives 1-2, 3-4, 5). Give exactly one of ranges or every. With output_dir the parts are written there as part-1.pdf, part-2.pdf, …; otherwise each part comes back inline as an application/pdf resource. Either way you also get a structured parts list (pages, page_count, bytes, and output_path or resource_uri). Existing part-N.pdf files with those names are overwritten, and part-N.pdf files from earlier runs in that directory are left as they are; the source is never modified. Limited to 100 parts and about 4 MB of total output; use pdf_extract_pages for a single range.

every.description: Chunk size in pages; the last part may be shorter

output_dir.description: Path of an existing directory inside the allowed directories (PDFOPS_ROOT, default the working directory) to write part-1.pdf, part-2.pdf, … into. Omit when running remotely: the parts are then returned inline as application/pdf resources.

password.description: Password to open the input, only needed for a user-password PDF (owner-locked files with an empty user password open without it).

pdf_path.description: PDF source: a path to a .pdf file inside the allowed directories (PDFOPS_ROOT, default the working directory), an https:// URL, or a data:application/pdf;base64,… URI. Use a URL or data URI when this server runs remotely (Smithery, hosted gateways) where local paths do not exist.

ranges.description: 1-based page spec; each comma group becomes one part, e.g. "1-2,3-5"

name: pdf_split

output_path.description: Absolute path written, when output_dir was supplied

resource_uri.description: pdfops:// uri of this part's inline application/pdf resource, when output_dir was omitted

title: Split PDF into parts
